messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] prod.streaming.tail_latency.p99 triggered at 1975009999 - p99 streaming tail latency > 5s in eu-west2. Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream. Paging oncall @oncall-elaine :rotating_light:

oncall-elaine: Oncall here, starting triage. Pulling Grafana and traces now. Ping if you see customer impact.

santiago: I see p95 jump ~800ms -> 450ms baseline, p99 ~5.8s. Streaming stalls: sessions show long tail stalls (10s-40s). Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/streaming?panelId=12 (link)

nima: Looking at network traces. High TLS handshake retries, SYN retransmits crossing AZ boundary (azb->azc). NAT gateway in eu-west2b showing high ephemeral port usage and conntrack table saturating.

ops_nora: CS update: a handful of live customers (3 accounts) reporting rebuffering and partial audio drop. Approx ~12% of active streaming sessions affected. No application 5xxs observed.

eng-sre-alex: Possible immediate mitigations we can do in parallel:
1) Scale dedicated streaming pool in eu-west2 (add 2 nodes) to reduce per-node KV/cache hotness.
2) Rotate NAT gateway (allocate new EIP / replace nat-gw) to clear conntrack state.
3) Apply temporary route rule to prefer same-AZ endpoints for streaming traffic (reduce cross-zone hairpin).
4) Reduce model throughput by falling back to smaller model variant for streaming routes to lower tokens/sec.

oncall-elaine: I'm going to take (1) and (2). Nima, can you prepare the route rule as a hotfix if things don't improve in 10-15m? I'll also enable model variant fallback for non-critical streams.

deploy-bot: Started scaling operation: dedicated-pool-streamer eu-west2 desired +2 (job id: deploy-1975009999-01)

oncall-elaine: Rotating NAT in eu-west2b now: creating replacement nat-gw -> new EIP, attaching to public route table. Will drain old gw after new is healthy.

nima: Preparing route rule: will add a policy to routing-plane to prefer AZ-local endpoints for /v1/stream via header-based affinity. Testing in staging now.

eng-sre-alex: Quick diagnostic snippets from nat-gw-eu-west2b before rotate:
```
# netstat snapshot
tcp        0      0 10.0.0.1:443        10.0.0.100:52344  TIME_WAIT
tcp        0      0 10.0.0.1:443        10.0.0.101:52345  TIME_WAIT
conntrack entries: 65534/65536
```

oncall-elaine: Scale job finished: +2 nodes active, health checks green.

deploy-bot: NAT rotate job started: nat-gw-eu-west2b -> nat-gw-1975009999-rot. Old gw being drained.

santiago: After scaling + nat rotate: p99 dropped from ~5.8s -> ~2.1s within ~4 minutes. p95 now ~420-480ms. Streaming stalls significantly reduced.

nima: TLS handshake error rate also down ~85% after NAT swap. Cross-AZ retransmit counts decreased. Looks like conntrack exhaustion + NAT path was the main amplifier.

ops_nora: Customer impact follow-up: CS will message impacted customers with a brief summary and ETA for full RCA. No escalations yet, one customer requested status updates.

oncall-elaine: Marking incident mitigated for live traffic. I'll handoff follow-up to eng-sre-alex for postmortem. Immediate next actions for follow-up:
- Root cause hypothesis: long-lived streaming sessions + NAT conntrack saturation during peak leading to TLS handshake spikes when sessions cross AZs.
- Short-term: per-AZ NAT pools or increase conntrack limit and implement sticky AZ routing for streaming.
- Long-term: evaluate dedicated NAT per streaming pool, connection reuse, and improve KV cache locality.

incidents-bot: Incident severity reduced to SEV2 at 1975010400. Paging cleared.

customer-success-lina: Thanks team — I'll update the customer-facing notes and include mitigation steps.

eng-sre-alex: I'll own the postmortem. Assigning action items: add automated alert for conntrack saturation, add runbook steps for NAT rotation, and test per-AZ routing policy.

oncall-elaine: Handoff to santiago for overnight follow-up. Please document any logs/time windows for postmortem (I exported p95/p99 series to /artifacts/1975009999/).

santiago: Got it. I'll validate histograms & traces and draft initial RCA.

oncall-elaine: Closing thread for active mitigation. If anything regresses ping @oncall-elaine or reopen the incident. Thanks all :heart:
